text: 🇲🇽⚽ FIFA World Cup tickets — high-cost by design — are being given away free to Mexican citizens. "The tickets FIFA delivered are being given to citizens, since they carry a high cost." — Mañanera, June 11 — World Cup ticket access program Cheapest FIFA tickets start at hundreds of dollars. Mexico's minimum wage is around $14 USD a day. The federal program closes the gap by routing tickets to youth, community athletes, and people who'd never otherwise get in.

🇲🇽✊ "Football is also health, community, and inclusion." IMSS-backed neighborhood tournaments. 6,875 community workdays organized to reclaim public courts and sports spaces. Categories for elders, women, kids — sport reaching people who historically had no access. — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director General The World Cup as the launch, not the destination. Public health, public space, public sport.

🇲🇽✊ Sheinbaum cuts out the middlemen on education reform — straight to teachers, school by school. "Starting in August, and let teachers know this — the consultation will be with them, directly, without intermediaries. We're going with the teachers, straight to them. Let the teachers decide." — Claudia Sheinbaum, June 11 mañanera The consultation will be conducted school by school, teacher by teacher. No fixed initiative — the policy comes out of the consultation itself, not from above.

🇲🇽⚽ "In this moment there are no longer any differences in Mexico. Mexico will win — it has the full support of the people." — Claudia Sheinbaum, opening day of the 2026 FIFA World Cup Mexico hosts its third World Cup today — the only country in history with that distinction. Inaugural match: Mexico vs. South Africa at Estadio Azteca, 11:30am.

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum hands Trump credit for USMCA — and reminds him whose deal it is to break. "USMCA was made by Trump. It is one of his best achievements. It is his. It benefits the three countries — not just Mexico or Canada. The strength of North America against other regions: it's better to be together." — Claudia Sheinbaum, June 11 mañanera Trump has spent months threatening tariffs. Sheinbaum's framing: the deal he wants to tear up is the one he built. North America's leverage against rival blocs is collective, not American.

🔥🇲🇽 "The far right means ending the people's rights." "It's very difficult for the far right to grow in Mexico. The far right means ending the people's rights." — Claudia Sheinbaum, June 11 mañanera Said in a country where minimum wage tripled since 2018, pensions are universal at 65, and scholarships run from preschool through university. The far-right pitch is austerity. Mexico chose the opposite — and keeps choosing it.

🇲🇽🛢️ Mexico and Brazil are linking up on deepwater oil — Pemex with Petrobras, two state companies, no privatization. "An agreement with Petrobras is about to be signed. They have very developed techniques for deep-water and ultra-deep-water exploration, and the objective is to sign an agreement with Pemex — joint work first, then possibly mixed exploitation of some of the wells." — Claudia Sheinbaum, after a call with Lula da Silva Petrobras leads the world in ultra-deepwater extraction. The pact starts with joint research and technology transfer in the Gulf of Mexico. Pemex stays public — South-South cooperation, no US majors.
